channel.title: Arizona Capitol Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Arizona Capitol Times (azcapitoltimes.com)

item.title: States target PBM pharmacy ownership in aggressive new push | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: State lawmakers are opening a new front in their battle with pharmacy benefit managers.

item.title: David Clouse: Law enforcement is a family tradition | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Public safety has been a lifelong mission for Navajo County Sheriff David Clouse, whose family has a history of serving in the county's Sheriff's Office.

item.title: City officials warn proposed tax freeze could jeopardize water projects | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Proposed tax freeze in Arizona could jeopardize water projects, city officials warn. Lawmakers' plan could limit ability to meet pressing needs.

item.title: HB 2375 preserves our historic districts, and that’s a good thing. | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: My community is not rich, racist, isolationist or unwelcoming. We want folks to join us in keeping historic districts alive and well.

item.title: Arizona lawyers up for potential Colorado River court battle | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Arizona is retaining legal counsel in preparation for a potential court battle over the Colorado River, according to Gov. Katie Hobbs’ office.

item.title: Proposed ballot measures would expand size of Legislature, shorten session | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Proposal to add 30 new House seats in Arizona aims to address district size and representation concerns. If approved, measure takes effect in 2043.

item.title: GOP bill would require voter approval of government surveillance | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Arizona lawmakers propose comprehensive regulation of government surveillance, requiring public vote and strict limits on data usage and retention.

item.title: Arizona Capitol Times – March 27, 2026 | Arizona Capitol Times
Women’s History Month: A conversation with Sen. Lela Alston | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Arizona's longest-serving legislator, Sen. Lela Alston, reflects on her time in office, her passion for education and senior citizens, and her plans for retirement.

item.title: Fontes lacked authority to OK Arizona Independent Party name change, judge rules | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Judge rules that Secretary of State Adrian Fontes lacked authority to approve Arizona Independent Party name change, calling it a political bait and switch.

item.title: Budget talks stall: Proposition 123 and tax conformity stay on standby | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Gov. Katie Hobbs and Republican lawmakers are in a budget battle over tax conformity and Prop. 123. Negotiations are on hold until a plan is presented.

item.title: Dueling proposals aim to resolve prison health care issues | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Two plans for a takeover of the Arizona Department of Corrections health care system are before a federal judge, but the state's appeal muddies the timeline.

item.title: Court considers state lawsuit against Saudi firm’s groundwater usage | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Judge considers halting lawsuit against Saudi-owned alfalfa farm as Arizona's water department moves to regulate groundwater use.

item.title: Arizona’s allied health care workforce could get needed boost from new bill | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Arizona faces a health care professional shortage, ranking ninth worst in the U.S. A proposed bill aims to establish a workforce development program to address the shortage.

item.title: Hand count immunity denied to Mohave County supervisor by Arizona Supreme Court | Arizona Capitol Times
item.description: Arizona Supreme Court denies immunity to Mohave County Supervisor Ron Gould for pursuing hand count of ballots, leaving the issue unresolved.
